'''Humiaki Huzita''' ([[Japanese language|Japanese]]: 藤田文章, [[Hepburn romanization]]: ''Fujita Fumiaki'') was a Japanese-born [[mathematician]] and [[origami]] artist who later became an Italian citizen. He was also a geologist and a physicist who focuses specifically on nuclear physics. Huzita is best known for formulating the first six [[Huzita–Hatori axioms]], which are rules associated with origami, the mathematics behind it, and the operations that form when folding a paper.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=David Lister on Humiaki Huzita|url=https://britishorigami.info/lister/humiaki_huzita.php|access-date=2021-12-11|website=britishorigami.info}}</ref>

== Biography and education ==
Humiaki Huzita was born in 1924 in [[Japan]]. After his basic education, he moved to [[Italy]] to attend the University of Padua. Here he studied nuclear physics and was eventually granted Italian citizenship.<ref name=":0" /> Though because of Japan's nationality laws, which do not allow dual citizenship, he was unable to live permanently in Japan following his retirement.<ref name=":0"/> Huzita, having lived in Japan and Italy, spoke both Japanese and Italian, however, he also spoke proficient English. This was advantageous for him and his cause, allowing him to spread his knowledge of [[origami]] and the geometry and mathematics behind it to a larger range of people.<ref name=":0" />

== Scientific career and contributions ==
Apart from origami, Humiaki Huzita studied nuclear physics.<ref name=":0" /> He has several publications on these topics. Some examples include the article "On the Analysis of the Slow Particles Emitted from Cosmic-Ray Stars" written with Shigeo Nakagawa, Eiji Tamai, and Kiyoaki Okudaira.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last1=Nakagawa|first1=Shigeo|last2=Tamai|first2=Eiji|last3=Huzita|first3=Humiaki|last4=Okudaira|first4=Kiyoaki|date=1956|title=On the Analysis of the Slow Particles Emitted from Cosmic-Ray Stars (I)|url=https://www.jstage.jst.go.jp/article/jpsj1946/11/3/11_3_191/_article/-char/ja/|journal=Journal of the Physical Society of Japan|volume=11|issue=3|pages=191–195|doi=10.1143/JPSJ.11.191|bibcode=1956JPSJ...11..191N}}</ref> This article discusses the measured diameter of the six unique tracks of stars ending in the G5 emulsion and the insights that this information gives.<ref name=":1" /> Another article on the topic of physics written by Humiaki Huzita is "Symmetry and Symmetry Breaking in Boats, its Propulsion Methods and Navigation Techniques."<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|last=Huzita|first=Humiaki|title=Symmetry and Symmetry Breaking in Boats, its Propulsion Methods and Navigation Techniques|url=http://www.scipress.org/journals/forma/pdf/1502/15020157.pdf|journal=INFN, Sezione di Padova|publisher=Univ. of Padova|location=Italy|archive-date=15 September 2012|access-date=11 December 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120915072825/http://www.scipress.org/journals/forma/pdf/1502/15020157.pdf|url-status=dead}}</ref> This article focusses on how symmetry breaking, or asymmetry, can sometimes be superior to symmetry even when unexpected, using boats as an example.<ref name=":2" /> One final example of an article by Huzita regarding nuclear physics is "Evidence of Non-Zero Mass Features for the Neutrinos Emitted at Supernova LMC-'87A."<ref>{{cite arXiv|last=Huzita|first=Humiaki|date=2002-12-23|title=Evidence of Non-Zero Mass Features for the Neutrinos Emitted at Supernova LMC-'87A|eprint=hep-ph/0212337 }}</ref>

Huzita was influential in the development of origami in Italy and internationally. For instance, Huzita invited [[Tomoko Fuse]] to the 1987 Italian Origami Society (Centro Diffusione Origami) convention in Padua because he noticed her talent, skill, and different origami techniques. Through her attendance at the convention, she began to gain worldwide recognition in the origami community.<ref name=":0" />  Huzita also organized several conventions and meetings between origami artists and mathematicians.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite book|last=Miura, Kawasaki, Tachi, Uehara, Lang, Wang-Iverson|title=Origami 6|year=2014}}</ref>  Huzita arranged "The First International Meeting of Origami Science and Technology” at the Casa di Ludovico Ariosto in [[Ferrara]], Italy.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3" /> This meeting had many origami mathematicians and artists from around the world and bridged the gap between them. On account of Huzita's pioneering idea for "The First International Meeting of Origami Science and Technology,” many more have followed since then. In 1994, a second conference was held in [[Ōtsu|Otsu, Japan]], followed by one in Asilomar, California, in 2001; [[Pasadena, California|Pasadena]], California, in 2006; [[Singapore]] in 2010; and [[Tokyo|Tokyo, Japan]], in 2014.<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":3" />

== Death ==
Humiaki Huzita died on March 26, 2005, due to an automobile accident.<ref name=":0" />
